headline: Commission reported scrapping Green Claims Directive as repairability consultation opens
summary: Reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon the Green Claims Directive, though general greenwashing rules remain active. Meanwhile, the Commission has opened a consultation on product repairability rules. Companies should also prepare supplier data collection for CSRD reporting starting in 2027.

items.title: Commission reportedly drops proposed Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission plans to withdraw the proposed Green Claims Directive, dropping planned ex-ante verification requirements for environmental claims.
items.meaning: While explicit pre-verification under this directive may be abandoned, green claims on your tools and packaging remain subject to general EU unfair commercial practices rules.
items.action: Maintain robust substantiation for existing green claims without preparing for formal ex-ante verification.

items.title: EU launches public consultation on product repairability rules
items.what: The European Commission has launched a public consultation to gather stakeholder feedback on strengthening EU product repairability requirements and reducing waste.
items.meaning: Future measures could introduce design, spare part availability, and technical information requirements for power tools and garden equipment sold in the EU.
items.action: Assess supplier repair capabilities and spare parts availability across your Chinese production bases.

items.title: Omnibus Reform clarifies CSRD and CSDDD application thresholds
items.what: Analysis clarifies ESG disclosure and due diligence rules under the Omnibus reform, outlining scope shifts for corporate sustainability reporting.
items.meaning: Your company falls inside the CSRD scope for financial year 2027, but remains outside direct CSDDD due diligence requirements.
items.action: Prepare Chinese supplier ESG data gathering to meet revised ESRS requirements starting in 2027.
